title: Biotechnology Toolkit Workflow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Biology
description: Interactive Mermaid workflow diagram comparing gene cloning and CRISPR gene editing pipelines with shared tools highlighted

learningObjectives: Organize the major biotechnology tools into a logical workflow
Explain how each tool contributes to a gene cloning or gene editing experiment
Compare gene cloning and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing pipelines
Identify shared tools used in both workflows

keyQuestions: What is the purpose of restriction enzymes in gene cloning?
How does CRISPR-Cas9 differ from traditional gene cloning?
Which tools are shared between gene cloning and gene editing?
When would you choose HDR over NHEJ for DNA repair?
commonMisconceptions: CRISPR and cloning are completely separate techniques with no shared tools
PCR is only used in gene editing, not in cloning
CRISPR always inserts new genes (it can also knock out or correct existing ones)
assessmentOpportunities: Identify which workflow to use for a given experimental goal
Explain the role of each shared tool in both contexts
